metadata.title: Adobe Integration with ChatGPT - Synthetic Persona Set
metadata.scope: Behavior-only persona testing for Adobe integration with ChatGPT

sharedTestContext.testingGoal: Evaluate how distinct synthetic users ask, refine, validate, and accept creative assistance through ChatGPT-connected Adobe workflows.
sharedTestContext.behaviorOnlyNote: These personas intentionally focus on observable behavior patterns only.

personas.name: Maya Srinivasan
personas.privacyPosture: Avoids uploading unreleased campaign data or confidential launch dates
personas.accessibilityNeeds: Prefers concise visual descriptions and strong text contrast reminders

behaviorProfile.decisionPattern: Chooses the fastest option that still looks polished
behaviorProfile.riskTolerance: Low for brand errors, medium for creative experimentation
behaviorProfile.collaborationPreference: Asks ChatGPT for quick options, then selects one to refine
acceptanceCriteria: Output feels campaign-ready
Text is short enough for social media
Visual direction is bright, optimistic, and easy to scan
No confidential product detail is exposed

behaviors.description: Starts with a compact instruction and asks for three creative directions before choosing one.
Refines quickly by changing color, headline length, and call-to-action wording one item at a time.
Checks whether the result is brand-safe, readable on mobile, and aligned with the campaign mood.
Replaces sensitive campaign names with placeholders and asks ChatGPT not to infer confidential details.

personas.name: Ethan Brooks
personas.privacyPosture: Does not share regulated client information, employee identifiers, or legal terms
personas.accessibilityNeeds: Needs plain-language explanations with minimal visual clutter

behaviorProfile.decisionPattern: Approves only after each risk item is addressed
behaviorProfile.collaborationPreference: Asks ChatGPT to state assumptions and provide review checkpoints
acceptanceCriteria: No legal, financial, or medical claims are invented
Design wording is neutral and non-promissory
Every suggestion is explainable
Sensitive details are excluded

behaviors.description: Begins by defining boundaries, restricted data, and required review checkpoints before asking for creative help.
Requests conservative alternatives and removes wording that could be interpreted as a claim.
Uses a pass/fail checklist for privacy, claim safety, accessibility, and audit readiness.
Flags anything uncertain for human compliance review instead of accepting ChatGPT's suggestion directly.

personas.name: Sofia Alvarez
personas.privacyPosture: Comfortable using public concept references but avoids client-only brand files
personas.accessibilityNeeds: Requests color contrast checks for final client handoff

behaviorProfile.decisionPattern: Explores divergent concepts before narrowing to one visual system
behaviorProfile.riskTolerance: High for aesthetics, medium for client-facing deliverables
behaviorProfile.collaborationPreference: Treats ChatGPT like a brainstorming partner and art-direction assistant
acceptanceCriteria: Design direction feels original
Composition has clear hierarchy
Color palette is intentional
Final wording can be reused in a client presentation
avoidList: Copying a known artist or living designer

behaviors.description: Uses mood words, layout references, and color intent to guide ChatGPT toward a distinct creative territory.
Asks for bold, moderate, and minimal versions so she can compare creative range.
Fine-tunes composition, negative space, typography mood, and visual rhythm across several short prompts.
Checks that the final concept feels ownable, not derivative, and can be explained to a client.

personas.name: Noah Kim
personas.privacyPosture: Avoids sharing student names, emails, and event registration data
personas.accessibilityNeeds: Needs accessible wording and readable poster text for campus displays

behaviorProfile.decisionPattern: Picks whatever is clearest to classmates and easiest to reuse
behaviorProfile.collaborationPreference: Uses ChatGPT to turn rough ideas into polished event material
acceptanceCriteria: Message is easy for students to understand
Design feels energetic but not chaotic
Important details are visible at a glance
No student personal data is used

behaviors.description: Starts with a rough idea and asks ChatGPT to make it clearer, more fun, and easier to turn into a campus graphic.
Changes wording based on whether friends would understand it in five seconds.
Checks event title, date, location placeholders, and readability before accepting the result.
Asks for versions that can work as both a poster and a social post.

personas.name: Priya Nair
personas.privacyPosture: Will not share supplier prices, customer lists, or revenue figures
personas.accessibilityNeeds: Prefers large text, clear buttons, and simple instructions

behaviorProfile.decisionPattern: Chooses options that are easy to edit again without expert help
behaviorProfile.collaborationPreference: Asks ChatGPT to explain each step before making another change
acceptanceCriteria: Instructions are simple enough to repeat
Design looks professional for local customers
Business details remain placeholders until final review
No hidden complexity is introduced

behaviors.description: Describes the business goal in plain language and asks for one recommended direction instead of many alternatives.
Requests numbered steps and confirms each edit before moving to the next.
Checks whether a non-designer could update the design later without breaking it.
Uses placeholders for prices, customer names, and supplier details until the final manual edit.

personas.name: Liam O'Connor
personas.privacyPosture: Strictly avoids credentials, internal URLs, tenant IDs, and employee records
personas.accessibilityNeeds: Requires keyboard-friendly workflow notes and accessible output checks

behaviorProfile.decisionPattern: Tests boundary conditions before trusting a workflow
behaviorProfile.riskTolerance: Low for data handling, medium for UI experimentation
behaviorProfile.collaborationPreference: Uses ChatGPT to model workflow behavior and identify operational risks
acceptanceCriteria: No secrets or identifiers are requested
Steps can be reproduced by another admin
Output respects enterprise policy language
Failure cases are acknowledged

behaviors.description: Provides structured constraints, allowed data types, and expected output format before asking ChatGPT to assist.
Attempts edge cases such as missing assets, restricted wording, or incomplete permissions.
Confirms that the workflow does not request credentials, private links, or internal identifiers.
Asks for reproducible steps that can be added to an internal test note.

personas.name: Aisha Bello
personas.privacyPosture: Protects beneficiary identities, donor details, and sensitive field locations
personas.accessibilityNeeds: Requests inclusive wording and readable designs for low-bandwidth sharing

behaviorProfile.decisionPattern: Balances emotional impact with dignity and consent
behaviorProfile.riskTolerance: Very low for privacy and representation, medium for storytelling style
behaviorProfile.collaborationPreference: Uses ChatGPT to improve clarity while preserving human dignity
acceptanceCriteria: Message is respectful and non-exploitative
No protected identity details are revealed
Call to action is clear
Design can be understood quickly on mobile
avoidList: Complex copy that weakens the call to action

behaviors.description: Frames the communication goal around dignity, consent, and community impact before asking for creative support.
Asks ChatGPT to flag wording that may feel exploitative, insensitive, or too donor-centric.
Adjusts tone until it feels hopeful, specific, and respectful.
Checks whether the final message is safe to share publicly without revealing protected details.

personas.name: Hiro Tanaka
personas.privacyPosture: Does not share factory layouts, machine identifiers, or proprietary process details
personas.accessibilityNeeds: Needs simple language, high contrast, and icon-friendly instructions

behaviorProfile.decisionPattern: Approves content only if it reduces ambiguity for trainees
behaviorProfile.collaborationPreference: Asks ChatGPT to simplify training language while preserving safety meaning
acceptanceCriteria: Instructions cannot be misread
Safety warnings are visible
No proprietary process details are exposed
Output is suitable for multilingual review

behaviors.description: States the training objective, safety priority, and restricted information before requesting a simplified creative draft.
Asks ChatGPT to identify any instruction that could be misunderstood by a new worker.
Rewrites each instruction into shorter, clearer, and more literal language.
Checks that the output can be reviewed by safety and localization teams.

personas.name: Grace Miller
personas.privacyPosture: Avoids sharing home addresses, phone numbers, and private community member details
personas.accessibilityNeeds: Needs larger text, simple layouts, and instructions without shortcuts

behaviorProfile.decisionPattern: Moves forward only when the next step feels clear
behaviorProfile.collaborationPreference: Asks ChatGPT for gentle guidance and simple wording
acceptanceCriteria: Instructions are easy to follow
Design does not feel crowded
Important details are large and readable
Private community details remain hidden

behaviors.description: Explains the goal in a conversational way and asks ChatGPT to guide her slowly.
Repeats back each instruction and asks if it is correct before continuing.
Requests simpler text, larger labels, and fewer visual elements when the result feels busy.
Checks whether another volunteer could understand and reuse the design without help.

personas.name: Marcus Reed
personas.privacyPosture: Does not share customer lists, private analytics exports, or unreleased roadmap details
personas.accessibilityNeeds: Requests contrast-aware variants for ads and landing page assets

behaviorProfile.decisionPattern: Compares variants and selects the one with the clearest hypothesis
behaviorProfile.collaborationPreference: Uses ChatGPT to generate test variants, hypotheses, and concise copy
acceptanceCriteria: Each variant has a clear test purpose
Copy is concise and measurable
No private metrics are exposed
Visual hierarchy supports quick scanning

behaviors.description: Provides the target audience, desired action, and testing hypothesis before requesting creative options.
Asks for multiple headline and layout variations that each test a different messaging angle.
Cuts copy aggressively, strengthens the call to action, and asks for sharper visual hierarchy.
Checks whether the result can be evaluated without inventing metrics or exposing private analytics.
